rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: Fed Oct hold ~83%, Dec hike ~94% (CME FedWatch); BoC Oct 28 hike ~80–85% (swaps/LSEG); RBNZ Oct 28 ~80%; BoE Nov 5 almost fully priced (LSEG); Greene: wage disinflation stalled; ECB/BoJ Dec likely
rows.read: The Fed's December hike stayed almost fully priced even as oil fell, so the US rate story held. Canada, New Zealand and Britain are still expected to hike first, and a hawkish Bank of England speaker backed the pound's case. Currencies whose banks are about to act keep the rate edge.

rows.figure: US housing starts 1.22M vs 1.30M fc; pending home sales -7.3% (record low); German ZEW 28.1 vs ~30 fc, EZ 18.5; UK unemployment 4.7%; US Russell 2000 +1.8%
rows.read: US housing is clearly weakening under high mortgage rates, which argues for a slower Fed and weighs a little on the dollar. German investors turned gloomier on high energy costs. Britain's job market still looks firm.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Greene: wage disinflation stalled above 2%-consistent levels; German PPI +6.7% y/y (morning); UK CPI Wed fc 3.4%; NZ Q3 CPI Wed fc 3.8%
rows.read: Energy is still the main source of inflation pressure, and today's oil drop was the first hint of relief. A Bank of England policymaker said pay growth has stopped cooling at too high a level. Wednesday's UK and New Zealand inflation reports are the next tests for rate bets.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: Reported Qatar–Pakistan framework (unconfirmed; diplomat: deal not close); DXY low ~101.5, lowest since Oct 1; Dow +1.0%, S&P +0.3%; Saudi TASI -1.1% on Houthi claims; Alberta ~76% remain
rows.read: Hope for US–Iran diplomacy calmed markets: stocks rose, oil fell and the dollar slipped. But nothing is confirmed, a diplomat said a deal is not close, and attacks around Saudi Arabia continue. Safe havens lost a little of their lift; the franc still holds firm against the euro on French worries.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.figure: Brent $108.79 settle (-0.7%; high $111.99); WTI Nov $101.79 at expiry, Dec $97.82; ≥18 vessels attacked in two weeks (Kpler); gold ~$4,121 (-0.5%); GDT whole milk powder +4.4%
rows.read: Oil swung from a five-month high to a loss on talk of diplomacy, though Gulf shipping is still badly disrupted. Cheaper oil helps importers like Japan and the euro area. Canada's currency gained anyway, because its rate story now matters more than the oil price.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: hedge funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against EUR (added), against NZD (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), oil bets near weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, and the loonie has now risen to a four-week high, which leaves those bets exposed. They also bet against the kiwi ahead of a likely hike. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors disagree.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.figure: France revenue vote moved to Oct 27 (amendments add ~€10B to deficit); France–Germany 10Y gap ~147bp (Mon); UK 10Y gilt auction 5.418%, cover 3.61x; Moody's France Fri; UK budget Oct 28
rows.read: France pushed its budget revenue vote back a week, so the risk to French bonds lingers without a verdict. Britain's 10-year bond sale went well, a calm read on UK debt before next week's budget. Moody's review of France on Friday is the next test for the euro.
